note: Licence text is what was read on the source page on the accessed date. 'not read' means the page could not be fetched or its terms text was not retrieved; those are treated as NOT allowed until read. Counts marked 'unmeasured' were not counted.

sources.title: Places theme (release 2026-10-21.0 named in the DuckDB docs)
sources.licence: "The theme is published under CDLA Permissive 2.0 and Apache 2.0, depending on the source"; page states it "contains no OpenStreetMap data and carries none of the share-alike obligations" of ODbL.
sources.coverage: Global points; ~88M records, Meta ~60M, BrightQuery ~16M, plus Microsoft, Foursquare, PinMeTo and others. Melbourne count unmeasured.
sources.fields: id (GERS), names, basic_category, taxonomy (OPC, ~2,300 categories), confidence 0-1, operating_status, addresses, websites, phones, socials, brand, sources[]. No opening hours, no price, no diet tags.
sources.size: Whole theme is tens of GB; a Greater Melbourne bbox food-category cut is expected to be megabytes (unmeasured).
sources.caveats: Docs say: "Places is known to contain duplicates, a high junk rate, and low property completeness." Confidence is "a relative filtering tool rather than a precise probability". 'categories' field removed from the schema as of the September 2026 release; use taxonomy.

sources.title: Attribution and licensing page (per-source licences)
sources.licence: Meta, Microsoft, PinMeTo, Krick, RenderSEO, DAC, BrightQuery, Birdeye, Uberall, OpenTravel Alliance: "Available under CDLA Permissive 2.0." Foursquare: "Copyright 2024 Foursquare Labs, Inc. All rights reserved. Available under Apache 2.0" with a NOTICE.txt. AllThePlaces: CC0 1.0. Suggested citation: "Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org" with the access date.

sources.title: Community Data License Agreement, Permissive, Version 2.0
sources.licence: Sharing allowed "so long as the Data Recipient makes available the text of this agreement with the shared Data"; "does not impose any restriction or obligations with respect to the use, modification, or sharing of Results"; no attribution requirement in the agreement.
sources.caveats: Publishing a places file means shipping the agreement text (or URL) with it. A short notice screen satisfies this.

sources.title: Places schema reference
sources.licence: Documentation; facts only used.
sources.fields: operating_status "does not indicate opening hours"; confidence 0 means permanently closed.

sources.title: overturemaps Python CLI and DuckDB access
sources.licence: Tooling documentation. CLI: overturemaps download --bbox=W,S,E,N -f geoparquet --type=place -o file; "Results are streamed, so arbitrarily large areas work"; only the minimum data is transferred for a bbox. DuckDB: SET s3_region='us-west-2'; read_parquet('s3://overturemaps-us-west-2/release/<release>/theme=places/type=place/*') filtered on bbox.xmin/bbox.ymin BETWEEN.

sources.title: Copyright and Licence
sources.licence: "Provide credit to OpenStreetMap by displaying our attribution notice"; "Make clear that the data is available under the Open Database License"; "if you alter or build upon the data, you may distribute the result only under the same license."
sources.coverage: Melbourne: rough Overpass count for shop=bakery|greengrocer|convenience|butcher in a Greater Melbourne box was about 1,718 nodes + 1,074 ways (relations not read). Restaurants/cafes and supermarkets not counted (Overpass was at capacity).
sources.fields: Free-form tags: name, amenity/shop, cuisine, diet:*, opening_hours, website, phone, addr:*. Completeness varies.
sources.size: Victoria extract 231 MB pbf (Geofabrik, data to 2026-10-28)

sources.title: ODbL 1.0 full text
sources.licence: Derivative Database: "a database based upon the Database, and includes any translation, adaptation, arrangement, modification". 4.4: "Any Derivative Database that You Publicly Use must be only under the terms of" ODbL (or compatible). 4.4(b): Extraction or Re-utilisation of the whole or a Substantial part of the Contents into a new database creates a Derivative Database. 4.5: using the database to create a Produced Work does not by itself create a Derivative Database; internal, non-public use of a Derivative Database does not trigger share-alike. Produced Works need a notice linking to the source database and stating the licence.

sources.title: Licence and Legal FAQ: Community Guidelines (Produced Work, Collective Database)
sources.licence: Guidance, not law. Produced Work is "something created from a database but not a database itself". If a data type consists entirely of non-OSM data within a regional cut, OSM and non-OSM datasets are treated as independent, so the combination is a Collective Database. Linked subpages for Geocoding and Derivative Database could not be read in full.

sources.title: Substantial guideline
sources.licence: "Less than 100 Features" one-off is not Substantial; systematic extraction such as "all eating places in an area" is Substantial; "repeated small extractions as one big extraction".

sources.title: Victoria extract
sources.licence: Page footer: "License: ODbL 1.0".

sources.title: Overpass API usage policy
sources.licence: Public instance: light use under 10,000 queries and 1 GB per day, "Commercial use should use self-hosted or paid Overpass servers"; results carry OSM's ODbL. Observed 2026-10-29: 502 at capacity.

sources.title: Cafe, restaurant, bistro seats (CLUE)
sources.licence: Portal API metadata: license "CC BY", licence_url https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode. Data Policy page itself returned 404.
sources.coverage: City of Melbourne local government area only (CBD, Southbank, Carlton, Docklands, etc.), annual census 2002-2024
sources.fields: trading_name, business_address, ANZSIC4 code and description, seating_type, number_of_seats, latitude, longitude, clue_small_area, census_year. No hours, no cuisine, no price.
sources.size: 66,356 rows across all years (one row per premises per seating type per year)
sources.caveats: Census-year snapshot: a place can have closed since. Some ANZSIC4 classes are retail (e.g. 'Other Specialised Food Retailing', Boost Juice).

sources.title: Bar, tavern, pub patron capacity
sources.licence: Portal API metadata: CC BY
sources.caveats: Not useful for cheap, healthy food; listed for completeness.

sources.title: Drinking fountains; Public barbecues
sources.licence: Portal API metadata: CC BY
sources.caveats: Free water is a real hunger-adjacent need but outside the food-places scope; optional later.

sources.title: Catalogue scan (238 datasets) for food, market, vendor, street food
sources.licence: Scanned titles via the portal catalogue API; no dataset titled markets, street food vendors or food premises was found. Only the five datasets in the entries above matched.

sources.title: Victorian liquor licences split by licence type
sources.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), as shown on the dataset page.
sources.coverage: Victoria-wide, 81 councils; includes Restaurant and cafe licence CSV
sources.fields: Licensee and business names, address, suburb, postcode, capacity, council, lat/long
sources.caveats: Licensed venues only, which skews to table-service dining and excludes most cheap takeaway. A cross-check for existence, not a source of cheap-food places.

sources.title: Registered food premises (Food Act 1984)
sources.licence: No open register found on data.vic.gov.au (search for food/market returned 0 datasets). Department of Health publishes only aggregate counts by council (107,063 registered premises in 2023). Registration is held by each council.
sources.caveats: Not allowed here means: no reusable place-level dataset exists, so nothing can be taken. Individual council registers, where public, would each need their own licence reading.

sources.title: Open Data Portal
sources.licence: Search results showed datasets under CC BY 2.5 Australia, and asset data under CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike). No food, market or community meal dataset found.
sources.caveats: Nothing on food found; check each dataset's own licence before use since some are CC BY-SA.

sources.publisher: Yarra, Darebin, Merri-bek, Maribyrnong, Brimbank, Greater Dandenong, Casey, Whitehorse, Monash, Boroondara
sources.title: Council open data portals
sources.licence: Not read. A search found no Yarra or Merri-bek open dataset on markets, food or community meals. Casey's list stays out per the earlier ruling (licence ambiguous).
sources.caveats: Nothing is usable until a dataset's licence is read on its own page. Council web pages listing community meals can still be used the way the existing 15 places are: facts only, read from the page.

sources.title: Wikidata licensing
sources.licence: "All structured data (i.e. the main, Property, Lexeme, and EntitySchema namespaces)" is CC0.
sources.coverage: Notable markets and some supermarkets only. A SPARQL count timed out on 2026-10-29 so no count is claimed.
sources.fields: Label, coordinates (P625), sometimes website and opening date
sources.caveats: Low volume. Good for coordinates of named markets, as already done.

sources.title: Find food locator and locations
sources.licence: No copyright or terms text found on the page footer. Locator is "Powered by Infoxchange". Charity Partner Terms (July 2024) bind partner charities, not users.
sources.caveats: No permission to copy the partner list. Do not scrape. Option: ask Foodbank Victoria / Infoxchange in writing, or link out to the locator. The same applies to SecondBite and OzHarvest (not read).

sources.title: Find a market (31 accredited markets per the site)
sources.licence: Terms not read; site is hosted on an iMIS domain and the apex domain did not resolve. Treated as operator page: facts only, read per market.
sources.coverage: 31 accredited markets across Victoria (Melbourne subset unmeasured)
sources.caveats: Facts-only reading per market from the operator or council page, same method as the existing markets. Do not bulk copy the directory text.

sources.title: Website terms and conditions
sources.licence: Users must not "copy, reproduce, republish, adapt" any part of the website or content; "personal purposes" only without written consent; no explicit scraping clause read.

sources.title: Website terms
sources.licence: Not read: both returned HTTP 403 or 404 to the fetch. Foodworks and IGA terms not read.
sources.caveats: Treated as not allowed until read. Supermarket chain locations come from Overture (brand field) instead.

sources.title: Places API policies
sources.licence: "You must not pre-fetch, cache, or store Places API content beyond the allowed exceptions"; only the place ID may be stored indefinitely.

sources.title: Developer terms
sources.licence: Not read (Yelp redirected and was not followed; others not fetched). Secondary sources say Yelp allows caching for 24 hours only and scraping breaches its terms.
sources.caveats: Treated as not allowed. Also each would be a third-party request at runtime, which the privacy rules forbid.
